title: Managing Victor's jazz repertoire in 1935; Rollini's tap room gang
summary: At Victor from 1935 he brought in jazz-minded groups, including Adrian Rollini's tap room gang with Fats Waller at the piano.

bands.name: Adrian Rollini and his Tap Room Gang

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom

blocks.x: I see. Yeah. Well, this, combining good jazz with commercial appeal, I think it deserves a great deal of attention. And you're being manager of the band, give you a little time to think about some of these things.

I'll say so. Well, the evolution of jazz in New York, you know, covers a big field. And when I joined Victor, as a manager of autism repertoire in 1935, my job then was to, to sort of lean over backward, to see if the, those people who were jazz minded, couldn't get more product. And it was then that I began bringing in bands in the Victor, for instance, Adrian Malini came in with a group, and he was playing at the Hickory House, not the Hickory House, but the, this, the present hotel. He had a little joint down there, and he had Fats Waller as pianist, in the, in, in the place. And, uh, uh, we called it, Adrian Malini, and just tap room gang. Adrian Malini and his tap room gang. So, uh, that's, uh, we made some records of Adrian, and, uh, and his tap room gang. Then, then we brought in, uh, uh, Joe Marcella, and, uh, made up a lot of groups, uh, to cater to the, the ever-growing demand for, for jazz records.
